chunks: And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The making up of the day prayer is permissible at any hour you wish, from the night or the day.'

key_terms.قَضَاؤُهَا: Making up / compensating for missed prayers

ai.seo_question: When can I make up missed day prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that the makeup (qada) of day prayers, such as Dhuhr and Asr, is not bound by the specific time windows of their original performance, allowing fulfillment at any hour of the night or day. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence for fulfilling obligatory duties when missed due to valid excuses, distinguishing it from the strict timing of the five daily prayers. It reflects the Imams' emphasis on the accessibility of worship, ensuring that believers are not burdened by rigid temporal constraints when making up missed obligations.
